entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Magnus of Trani was a 3rd-century Roman Catholic saint born in unknown circumstances and died on August 19, 251. He is venerated as the patron saint of Anagni in the Province of Frosinone (Lazio), together with his apprentice Saint Secundina, and also associated with the church of Santi Michele e Magno in Rome.

Magnus played a significant role in the early Christian Church, serving as bishop of Trani and later of Anagni. His legacy has endured for centuries, with his relics being relocated to St. Peter's Basilica in 1901.

The Saint Magnus of Trani's story is also intertwined with the legend of Saint Secundina, who accompanied him on many of his missionary journeys. The two saints are considered one of the most revered and influential figures in the history of Christianity, particularly in the region of Lazio.

Magnus' historical significance extends beyond his own lifetime, as he represents a pivotal moment in the development of early Christian theology and practice. His contributions to the Church's growth and spread have had a lasting impact on Western civilization.
